evidence.observation: The lifecycle helper's rest state is fully defined here: stop_event=None, watcher_thread=None, changed_files=set() and gitignore_spec=None when no gitignores are supplied. These three attributes are the observable state that the state-transition test classifies as 'idle', so the initial-state assertions (test_fresh_watcher_is_idle) are grounded in this constructor.

start() implements the sole 'idle -> running' legal edge: it allocates a fresh threading.Event (stop_event), resets changed_files, and spawns a daemon thread running watch_files(). It does NOT guard against being called while already running, which is the illegal-edge hazard the transition test documents (double start abandons the previous session's thread and stop_event references).

stop() implements the 'running -> idle' legal edge and is written defensively: both `if self.stop_event:` and `if self.watcher_thread:` guards make stop() a safe no-op when the helper was never started or is already stopped, and a second stop() is idempotent. This is exactly the tolerated-illegal-edge behaviour asserted by test_illegal_edge_stop_before_start_is_tolerated and test_illegal_edge_double_stop_is_idempotent.

handle_changes() is the command edge of the session lifecycle. An empty/falsy batch is a legal no-op returning False; a non-empty batch normalizes each change to str(Path(change[1])), merges into changed_files, signals io.interrupt_input() and returns True, keeping the session in 'running'. A malformed change with no path component (change[1] missing) is rejected with IndexError/TypeError instead of silently recording a bogus file, which the illegal-edge test asserts.

watch_files() is the thread body that consumes the watchfiles backend and composes the two edges: it calls handle_changes() on each change batch and returns as soon as handle_changes() reports True. test_watch_files_forwards_first_change_batch exercises this by driving a scripted 'watch' generator and asserting the batch is folded into changed_files and io.interrupt_input is signalled.

The existing acceptance test's fixture collaboration object shows how FileWatcher is driven in this repo: a minimal coder exposing io, root and abs_fnames and a get_rel_fname passthrough. The new state-transition test mirrors this shape (FakeCoder/FakeIO) so it stays faithful to the repository's established test contract while avoiding the heavy aider.io import.

This is the existing precedent for constructing a FileWatcher directly against a tmp_path root (FileWatcher(coder, root=tmp_path)) and asserting on its lifecycle-adjacent output. The new test reuses the same construction contract (root=tmp_path) for its idle/running transitions.

The repository's existing (single-edge) test for the command edge already pins handle_changes([]) -> False with unchanged changed_files and handle_changes([('modified', path)]) -> True with changed_files growing by one. The new state-transition test generalizes this exact contract into a full legal/illegal edge table and adds the running-session and interrupt_input assertions.

claims.claim: FileWatcher.start() is the only legal 'idle -> running' transition: it installs a threading.Event into stop_event, clears changed_files, and spawns a daemon watcher thread, so the helper's observable state flips from idle to running.
FileWatcher.stop() implements the legal 'running -> idle' transition and also tolerates the illegal edges stop-before-start and double-stop as guarded, idempotent no-ops rather than raising.

FileWatcher.handle_changes() is the session's command edge: an empty batch is a legal no-op (False, state unchanged), a non-empty batch updates changed_files, signals io.interrupt_input and returns True while staying running, and a malformed change lacking a path component is deterministically rejected.

FileWatcher.watch_files() composes start()/stop() with handle_changes() by returning on the first handled batch, and FileWatcher.__init__ fixes the idle baseline state (stop_event/watch_thread None, changed_files empty) that the transition table starts from.

The repository already establishes the public contract for this helper through test_handle_changes (empty vs non-empty batch) and test_get_roots_to_watch/MinimalCoder (direct construction with root=tmp_path); the new state-transition test extends, rather than contradicts, that contract.

The new executable demo tests/basic/test_watch_lifecycle_transitions.py drives the real FileWatcher source through a legal-edge table (start, stop, changes, nochange) and an illegal-edge table (stop-before-start, nochange-before-start, double-stop, double-start, malformed change), asserting document state and side effects on every edge.

conclusion: The watch/session lifecycle helper in aider/watch.py is FileWatcher. Its lifecycle is a two-state machine (idle <-> running) joined by the handle_changes() command edge. Legal edges are fully specified: start() enters running and resets per-session state, stop() returns to idle, and handle_changes() keeps the session running while folding detected paths into changed_files and signalling io.interrupt_input. Illegal edges split into two classes: tolerated ones (stop before start, double stop, empty/None batch, and even changes before start) which are guarded no-ops that preserve state, and one genuinely unsafe illegal edge -- a second start() while running abandons the prior session's thread and stop_event with no recovery path from stop() -- plus malformed change entries, which are deterministically rejected. The delivered state-transition test (tests/basic/test_watch_lifecycle_transitions.py) encodes this contract as executable assertions over both edge tables, 19 cases, all passing. Optional test dependencies (grep_ast, watchfiles, oslex) are absent in this workspace, so the demo stubs the two module-import-time watch dependencies and always scripts the watch() backend; this is recorded as the validation limitation rather than installed.

validation.notes: 19 passed in 0.10s. Focused run of the new state-transition demo against the real FileWatcher source in aider/watch.py. LIMITATION: the optional dependencies grep_ast, watchfiles (needed to import aider/watch.py) and oslex (needed to import aider.io, hence tests/basic/test_watch.py) are NOT installed in this workspace and were deliberately not installed, per the no-install rule. Consequently (a) the demo injects minimal stubs for grep_ast/watchfiles only at import time and replaces the watch() backend with a deterministic scripted generator, so the lifecycle methods themselves run unmodified; and (b) the repository's own tests/basic/test_watch.py cannot be collected here (ImportError: oslex / grep_ast), so it is cited as the acceptance contract via static inspection rather than execution.
